tool.name: INaturalistObservations

summary.para:
View online help files: https://www.jennessent.com/data-tools/inaturalist-observations.html
Gets observations straight from iNaturalist.org and writes them as a point feature class, for the species or groups, study area or named place, dates and quality grades you choose. GBIF holds only part of iNaturalist: the research-grade observations whose observers chose a CC0, CC BY or CC BY-NC license. This tool also reaches the observations that still need an identification, the casual ones and the ones under other terms, and it carries fields GBIF does not: how many identifiers agreed and disagreed, the annotations (life stage, sex, alive or dead, evidence of presence), whether the location was obscured, and whether iNaturalist lists the taxon as native or introduced where it was seen. No account is needed. Works at every license level.

tool.usage:
iNaturalist or GBIF. iNaturalist publishes its research-grade observations under the CC0, CC BY and CC BY-NC licenses to GBIF, where the GBIF Species Occurrences tool gets them together with museum specimens and other sources, in any number, and with a DOI to cite. Use this tool when you want what GBIF does not have: observations that are not yet research grade, observations under other terms, and iNaturalist's own fields. The two tools give the same names to the fields that mean the same thing (scientificName, species, kingdom to genus, eventDate, year, month, day, decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, coordUncert_m, recordedBy, license, recordURL).
Quality grades. An observation is research grade when it has a date, a location, a photograph or sound, is of a wild organism, and is identified to species or finer with more than two-thirds of its identifiers agreeing. Needs ID observations meet the same conditions but the community has not yet agreed on an identification. Casual observations lack a date, a location or a photograph or sound, or are of a captive or cultivated organism, or were voted down. Only research grade is chosen at first. Identifications on iNaturalist are made by volunteers, so even a research-grade identification is an agreement, not a review by an expert.
Obscured locations. iNaturalist hides the true location of observations of species at risk, and of any observation whose observer asks for it. The location it shows instead is a random point within the cell of about 0.2 degrees of latitude and longitude that holds the true one, so the point can be as much as about 30 kilometers from where the organism was. Those points are written, with obscured set to Yes and the size of the area in coordUncert_m, and the tool's messages count them. Leave them out with the option for it, or select them afterwards. Observations whose observer set the location to private have no coordinates at all and are never written.
The study area. iNaturalist searches by rectangle or by one of its own named places, never by polygon. For a polygon study area the tool asks for the rectangle around the polygons and then cuts the observations to the polygons, so the count iNaturalist reports is for the rectangle and the number written is smaller. A named place (a country, state, county, park and so on) is searched exactly, by iNaturalist's own boundary for it. Give a place by name as iNaturalist writes it (Arizona, US), or by its place id. A study area and a place can be given together; the observations are then those in both.
Names. A species or group is given by its scientific name, its common name, or its iNaturalist taxon id; a group (a genus, a family, Mammalia) brings every species in it. A name must match exactly one taxon. If it matches none or several, the tool stops and lists the closest taxa with their ids. iNaturalist's taxon ids are its own, not GBIF's taxon keys.
How many, and how long. iNaturalist's service gives 200 observations a request. iNaturalist asks for no more than 60 requests a minute and fewer than 10,000 a day, which is 2,000,000 observations, and it says the service is meant for applications and not for copying its data in bulk. The tool makes no more than one request a second, so 10,000 observations take about two minutes, 100,000 about twenty and a million about three hours. When more than 100,000 observations match, the tool warns you and says how long the fetch will take, and you can cancel it at any time. When more than 2,000,000 match, the tool stops before fetching anything. That limit is iNaturalist's 10,000 requests a day. It is there to respect iNaturalist's intent for its service, and to protect you: iNaturalist says it may block, without notice, a computer that goes beyond what it asks. Narrowing the species, the area, the dates or the grades shortens it, and for research-grade observations in bulk the GBIF Species Occurrences tool can request a download of any size.
Native or introduced. The native, introduced, endemic and threatened fields are what iNaturalist's own lists say of the taxon at the place of the observation. They are kept by its community and are not complete for every place.
Licenses and citation. Every observation carries the license its observer chose, in the license field; where the observer chose none, all rights are reserved and the field says so. The first photograph's license is given separately, because it can differ. The messages count the observations under each license and give the citation in the form iNaturalist asks for. iNaturalist prefers that research cite a GBIF download where it can.
The window or the tool. The iNaturalist Observations window (Data Tools group, Online Data) finds species and places by name and counts the matching observations as you choose. Its last step runs this tool. To automate a request, make it once in the window, then right-click its entry in the Geoprocessing History and choose Copy Python Command.

param.name: taxa
param.displayname: Species or groups (scientific or common names, or iNaturalist taxon ids, separated by semicolons)

dialogReference.para: One or more species or groups, separated by semicolons. Each is a scientific name (Antilocapra americana), a common name (pronghorn), an iNaturalist taxon id (42429), or a name followed by its id in brackets (Pronghorn (42429)), in which case the id is used. A group such as a genus, a family or Mammalia brings every species in it. Empty for all species.

A polygon layer or feature class. Selected polygons are used when there is a selection, and a definition query is honored. The observations are asked for in the rectangle around the polygons and cut to the polygons when they are written.

param.name: extent
param.displayname: Or a rectangle as the study area

dialogReference.para: A rectangle, in any coordinate system. Give a study area layer or a rectangle, not both.

param.name: place
param.displayname: Or an iNaturalist place (its name, such as Arizona, US, or its place id)

dialogReference.para: One of iNaturalist's named places: a country, state, county, park or a place its community has drawn. Give its name as iNaturalist writes it (Arizona, US or Coconino County, US, AZ) or its place id (40). If the name matches several places, the tool stops and lists them with their ids. The place's own boundary is used, so no polygon layer is needed.

bulletList.bullet_item: Research grade: dated, located, with a photograph or sound, of a wild organism, and identified to species or finer with more than two-thirds of the identifiers agreeing. The default.
Needs ID: meets the same conditions, but the community has not yet agreed on an identification.
Casual: lacks a date, a location or a photograph or sound, or is of a captive or cultivated organism, or was voted down.

param.name: exclude_captive
param.displayname: Leave out captive or cultivated organisms

dialogReference.para: Checked, pets, zoo animals, garden plants and other organisms that are where they are because people put them there are left out. They are always casual grade, so this matters only when Casual is among the quality grades.
Leave out observations made before this date. Empty for no limit.
Leave out observations made after this date. Empty for no limit.
The months of the year to keep (1 to 12), in every year. Empty for all months.

param.name: open_license_only
param.displayname: Only observations under CC0 or a Creative Commons license

dialogReference.para: Checked, observations whose observers gave no license (all rights reserved) are left out.

param.name: exclude_noncommercial
param.displayname: Only observations whose license allows commercial use

dialogReference.para: Checked, only observations under CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA or CC BY-ND are kept. Most iNaturalist observations are licensed for non-commercial use only, so this leaves out most of them.
Checked, observations without a photograph are left out.

Keep only observations whose observer stated a location accuracy of less than this many meters. Observations that state no accuracy are left out. For an obscured observation the stated accuracy describes the hidden true location, not the point that is written, so combine this with the option to leave out obscured observations.

param.name: exclude_obscured
param.displayname: Leave out observations whose location is obscured

dialogReference.para: Checked, observations whose public location is a random point (species at risk, and observers who chose to hide the place) are left out. Unchecked, they are written with the obscured field set to Yes. Leaving them out removes most observations of species at risk.

param.name: establishment
param.displayname: Native or introduced (as iNaturalist lists the taxon for the place of the observation)

bulletList.bullet_item: Native: only taxa iNaturalist lists as native to the place of the observation.
Introduced: only taxa iNaturalist lists as introduced there.

dialogReference.para: The login name of one iNaturalist user, to get that person's observations only.

param.name: project
param.displayname: Only this iNaturalist project (the last part of its web address, or its id)

dialogReference.para: One iNaturalist project, named by the last part of its web address (for inaturalist.org/projects/my-class-bioblitz, give my-class-bioblitz) or by its id.

param.name: out_features
param.displayname: Output point feature class (in a file geodatabase)

dialogReference.para: The point feature class to create, directly inside a file geodatabase (not in a feature dataset). The field names are too long for a shapefile. Coordinates are WGS 84.
The number of points in the output.

scriptExample.title: iNaturalist Observations example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: Research-grade pronghorn observations in Arizona, by iNaturalist's own boundary for the state.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.jenness.INaturalistObservations( taxa="Antilocapra americana", place="Arizona, US", out_features=r"D:\data\wildlife.gdb\Pronghorn_iNat")

scriptExample.title: Every mammal observation in a study area, whatever its grade
scriptExample.para: All quality grades in the polygons of a layer, for one year, without the obscured locations.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.jenness.INaturalistObservations( taxa="Mammalia", study_area=r"D:\data\wildlife.gdb\Study_Area", quality_grades="'Research grade';'Needs ID';Casual", date_from="2025-01-01", date_to="2025-12-31", exclude_obscured=True, out_features=r"D:\data\wildlife.gdb\Mammals_iNat_2025")
